Accomplish
ak-kŏm´plĭsh
v. (to complete, fulfil; rendering Hebrew kalah, Greek teleo)
From Latin ad and complere, to fill up. To accomplish is to fill out what was begun until nothing remains outstanding.

Biblical Definition

To accomplish is to complete. God says of His word, “it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it” (Isa 55:11). Daniel understands by books “the number of the years… that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem” (Dan 9:2). Luke says Moses and Elijah on the mount spoke of Christ's decease “which he should accomplish at Jerusalem” (Luk 9:31).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines accomplish as to complete; to finish entirely; to execute; to fulfill; to carry into effect; and to gain, to obtain or effect by successful exertions.

expand to see more

ACCOMPLISH, v.t. To complete; to finish entirely.

2. To execute; as to accomplish a vow, wrath or fury.

3. To gain; to obtain or effect by successful exertions.

4. To fulfill or bring to pass; as, to accomplish a prophecy.

5. To furnish with qualities which serve to render the mind or body complete.

Key Scripture

Isa 55:11 — "So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it."

Dan 9:2 — "In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem."

Luk 9:31 — "Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem."

Isa 55:10 — "For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater:"

Modern Corruption

Preaching is judged by visible response, and Isaiah attaches the guarantee to the word itself rather than to the audience.

expand to see more

Isaiah 55:11 is the preacher's warrant and it contains no clause about reception: so shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it. The word accomplishes what God pleases, which is not always what the speaker hoped. Isaiah himself was told to preach to people who would not hear, and the promise held for him too.

Luke 9:31 uses the word of the crucifixion, and the choice is striking: they spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem. Not suffer, not undergo — accomplish. Moses and Elijah discussed the cross with Him as a work to be completed. That single verb rules out any reading of Calvary as a tragedy that overtook Him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kalah (H3615), to complete, finish; tsalach (H6743), to prosper; Greek teleo (G5055), to finish; pleroo (G4137), to fulfil.

expand to see more

Hebrew kalah (H3615) — to accomplish, complete; Daniel 9:2, 2 Chronicles 36:21.

Hebrew asah (H6213) — to do, accomplish; Isaiah 55:11, it shall accomplish that which I please.

Greek pleroo (G4137) — to fulfil, accomplish; Luke 9:31, Acts 13:33.

Usage

"“It shall accomplish that which I please” — no clause about reception."

"“His decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem” — a work completed, not a fate suffered."

"“He would accomplish seventy years” — Daniel reading a deadline in a book."
